It occurs to me that a lot of comments (today and often) are not “this is a bad puzzle” but “this is a bad puzzle because today is the wrong day for it”. 

This seems unduly harsh in terms of the message it sends to the constructor. We may love a puzzle but hate it because it’s too hard or too easy.  Perhaps we should temper our “wrong day” gripes with a word of appreciation, if we have one. 

I feel that our “wrong day” comments are akin to a Frenchman who goes to the same bistro for lunch every day, and complains to the garçon: “Mais cette omelette n’est pas une omelette du mercredi!”

Now that’s a one-of-a-kind theme, and it’s tight as well.  One of my favorite parts of the solving experience today was mulling the theme over post-solve and marveling at how unique it is.

One of its lovely aspects is that the first word of each theme answer is a verb, but in the original “X and Y” phrase, it is not.  For example, FAST is a verb in FAST LOOSELY, but in “fast and loose” it is an adjective.

That makes me go “Huh!” and “Wow!” at the same time.

I liked the variety of splat-fill in some areas and rub in others.  Plus, some sweet serendipities – crossing rhymes (TRECK and DRECK, AWAIT and MATE), not to mention SHOW abutting TUNE.

This is Karen’s third puzzle, and her first two had the same wonderfully quirky feel as today’s.

It’s nice to see you here again, Karen, after an absence of four years, and it’s always terrific to see a promising debut, as this is for you, Peter.  Thank you both for one terrific Tuesday!

I paused, a little bit perplexed, over CLEAN SOBERLY because it's a phrase that's not in the language.  I was off in the East, when it suddenly occurred to me: "But CLEAN AND SOBER is!"After which, I immediately thought of FAST AND LOOSE, LEFT AND RIGHT, and SHORT AND SWEET as soon as I saw the first word.  I not only love the punny wordplay, but I love the way the noun has been turned into a verb in the adverbial phrase.  Delightful -- and the cluing is terrific.  Why?  Out of context, the clues seem peculiar and eccentric, but when you know the trick, they're remarkably accurate and fair.

And such a clean grid!  No names, no crosswordese.  I'm going to make a bet here:  I'm going to bet that this puzzle will not garner a single negative review.  Not even one.  It's breezy and lighthearted and fun -- and I bet everyone else loved it too.  Great Tuesday!
